headline: High: kotaemon’s broad egress and API-key handling can leak sensitive documents, while shared file/workspace use creates prompt-injection and cascading-error risks with godot_rl_agents.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: kotaemon ingests documents/HTML/PDFs and serves them through a web UI, so attacker-controlled content can reach its outputs. godot_rl_agents has no documented input bridge, but if its outputs are copied into kotaemon or a shared workspace is used, prompt injection becomes plausible. The interaction is inferred from docs, not directly observed.
conditions: IF the two agents share a filesystem or copy-paste bridge
IF kotaemon renders untrusted document text into prompts or answers without provenance filtering
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents
Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted documents in kotaemon
Add provenance labels to imported text
Review any copied agent output before pasting
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and prompt-boundary enforcement

B_data_leakage.rationale: kotaemon touches documents, chat transcripts, and API keys and has broad network egress to third-party APIs, so sensitive content can leave the local boundary by default. godot_rl_agents is network-egress none, so it is not the leak source; the pairwise risk is that kotaemon can exfiltrate shared data while the other agent cannot contain it. This is a docs-only inference, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF kotaemon is configured with any external LLM/API backend
IF sensitive documents or API keys are placed in kotaemon's workspace
mitigations: Keep secrets out of kotaemon-managed files
Use a local-only backend in kotaemon
Restrict the shared workspace to non-sensitive documents
Rotate any API keys exposed to the workspace
requires-engineering: enforce egress allowlists and secret redaction

C_capability_conflict.rationale: kotaemon supports multiple instances and writes to ./ktem_app_data, while godot_rl_agents has no documented write surface. There is no direct evidence of overlapping writes, but if both are pointed at the same directory or shared mutable resource, conflicts can corrupt state. Because the write surface is only documented for one agent, uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same directory or git repository
IF kotaemon runs multiple instances against one shared state directory
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Avoid shared git working trees
Run only one writer per workspace
Back up state before concurrent runs
requires-engineering: add file locking or transactional writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: kotaemon is a customer-support/RAG system that can turn retrieved text into answers, so if godot_rl_agents output is fed into it, downstream users may treat unverified content as authoritative. godot_rl_agents has no verification or citation surface documented, and kotaemon’s web UI can present results directly. The pathway exists by inference, not direct evidence, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF outputs from godot_rl_agents are ingested into kotaemon as source material
IF kotaemon presents retrieved/generated text without a human verification step
mitigations: Mark agent-generated text as unverified
Require human review before acting on answers
Separate retrieval sources from action logs
Add citation checks in kotaemon
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: kotaemon explicitly handles documents, chat transcripts, and API keys and uses external APIs, while godot_rl_agents is open-source game-playing with no data classes touched. The compliance concern is one-sided: if regulated or sensitive documents are loaded into kotaemon, retention and residency obligations may be triggered. No direct residency mismatch is documented, so medium fits.
conditions: IF regulated documents, chat transcripts, or API keys are processed in kotaemon
IF the deployment uses a third-party API backend outside the required jurisdiction
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of kotaemon
Configure retention to the minimum needed
Use region-matched API endpoints
Document data-processing roles and retention
requires-engineering: implement residency and deletion controls
